summary: Explains that a BGP speaker can apply RPKI origin validation to routes it sends as well as routes it receives. For such export checks, the classification should use the effective origin AS, which can be changed by features like removing private ASes or confederation handling. It updates RFC 6811 and is standards-track.

plainLanguage.summary: A BGP router can check the origin of routes it sends to its neighbors, as well as routes it receives. For an outgoing route, it must check the origin AS that remains after outbound changes are applied.

subtitle: Apply RPKI origin validation to outgoing BGP routes using their effective origin AS.

tldr.problem: Outbound BGP policy can change a route's origin AS, so validating the route before those changes can produce the wrong state.
tldr.mechanism: A validating speaker MUST apply origin validation after egress configuration and policy, using the origin AS that the outgoing UPDATE will carry.
tldr.outcome: This RFC updates RFC 6811 and adds no IANA actions.

today: RFC 8893 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6811. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Origin Validation on Export
sections.content:
This document does not change the protocol or semantics of BGP prefix origin validation in RFC 6811. It clarifies how to use that validation in external BGP (eBGP) egress policy.

The validation state for an outgoing route must be based on its effective origin Autonomous System Number (AS), the origin in the UPDATE that will be sent to the neighbor.
sections.plainLanguage: Origin validation can also be applied to routes a router sends out. It needs to assess the route as it will appear to the neighbor.

sections.title: The Effective Origin AS
sections.content:
The effective origin AS is determined by the speaker's configuration and outbound policy. It can differ from the route's origin in the routing information base (RIB).

Removing private ASes, handling confederations, migration, and other AS_PATH changes can alter the effective origin AS. A validating speaker MUST take those changes into account and apply validation after egress configuration and policy.
sections.plainLanguage: Outbound policy can change which AS appears as the route's origin. Check that final AS, not an earlier version of the route.

sections.title: Egress Policy Processing
sections.content:
Implementations that support RPKI origin validation MUST provide the same policy configuration primitives for validation decisions in ingress, redistribution and egress policies.

For egress, the validation state MUST use the effective origin AS of the route as it will or would be announced. The RFC says this can improve protection for outbound eBGP compared with relying only on ingress or redistribution checks.
sections.plainLanguage: Routers must offer the same validation controls for incoming, redistributed, and outgoing routes. For outgoing routes, apply the check using the final announced origin.

sections.title: Operational Considerations
sections.content:
Complex outbound policies may make the effective origin AS hard to know until those policies have run. It SHOULD be possible to apply a selective origin validation policy after existing non-validating outbound policies.

An implementation SHOULD be able to list announcements it did not send, such as routes marked Invalid, while those announcements remain in memory.
sections.plainLanguage: Run the validation after outbound rules that might change the origin AS. It should also be possible to inspect routes that were held back.

references.text: Mohapatra, P., Scudder, J., Ward, D., Bush, R., and R. Austein, "BGP Prefix Origin Validation", RFC 6811, January 2013.
Bush, R., "Clarifications to BGP Origin Validation Based on Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI)", RFC 8481, September 2018.
